targets.Description: The SCF is the only member-led organisation dedicated to promoting crofting and it is the largest association of small scale food producers in the UK. Their mission is to safeguard and promote the rights, livelihoods and culture of crofters and their communities. They work to develop, promote and encourage crofting; represent and safeguard the interests of crofters, their families and communities, their cultural heritage and their legislative rights; promote the environmental, social and cultural benefits of crofting activity and land use as intrinsic aspects of rural development; raise awareness of crofting through information and education; and promote diversity of people, enterprise, skills and expertise. Established and run by crofters themselves, the SCF actively engages with agencies and government officials at local, national and international levels to influence policy on rural, agricultural, social, environmental and other issues.
The Soil Association is the UK’s leading membership charity campaigning for healthy, humane and sustainable food, farming and land use.

Slow Food is a global, grassroots movement with thousands of members around the world that links the pleasure of food with a commitment to community and the environment. It was founded in 1989 in Italy. It is a not–for–profit organisation seeking to promote a better way to eat, celebrating the rich food traditions of the UK and protecting our edible biodiversity.

Website for Farming Futures, a resource for farmers, land managers and their advisers on the issues of climate change and sustainability in agriculture. Farming Futures is a consortium initiative currently led by Aberystwyth University and Harper Adams University.
Visit My Farm is an organisation for farmers looking for help about educational visits to farms and the countryside.

Stepney City Farm in London’s East End is a working farm, Rural Arts Centre and community meeting place. They give children and adults a chance to meet farm animals, learn how to grow food and try out arts and crafts.

Vauxhall City Farm is the most centrally located farm in London. They specialise in educational, recreational and therapeutic services and activities ranging from school trips, workshops, gardening projects and birthday parties to Riding for the Disabled.

Stonehouse Farm is located in West Harling, Norfolk. They are a mixed livestock farm producing high genetic value breeding animals. They run 1200 breeding sheep including pedigree Lleyns and 150 suckler cows, all put to Stabiliser bulls, across more than 2500 acres of organic land. The key to the business is maximising the value of the animals as they are run on some of the poorest land in the country.

targets.Description: Chagfarm (Chagford Community Farm CIC) aims to make the local community's food supply more resilient by working closely with Chagfood, another local food enterprise, and complementing their existing vegetable subscription offer. They do this by offering local goat dairy products and honey, as well as high-welfare goat meat, pork, organic woodland poultry, lamb, beef, venison and game. They operate on a payment by subscription basis, meaning customers sign up as members and commit to buying a certain amount of produce over a period of at least a year. Their mission is to develop a thriving local economy by supporting existing producers and retailers, including working with local butchers and offering produce from other farms.

Chagfood is one of a growing number of Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) schemes across the UK that directly connect consumers and the farmers who produce their food. CSA simply describes a model of subscription farming where customers commit to support a farm for an entire season by paying for their produce either up front or by monthly direct debit. From the farmer’s point of view this commitment provides a guaranteed market and allows us to farm in a more low-input ecological way. In return members have a direct connection to the people and the fields producing their food and the opportunity to get involved with how their food is produced. At Chagfood, they offer our members a ‘share’ of the harvest over the entire growing season for a set price. CSA is about consumers & farmers sharing the rewards and the risks of farming between them.

Chantry Farm is a campsite in the South East of England, consisting of 54 acres on the South Downs. They promote walks in the country to see skylarks, sheep and other guests. The campers help fund the farm restoration. Chantry dates back to 1350. Campers also help fund Chantry Farm to undertake small scale local food production.

LEAF Open Farm Sunday, is managed by LEAF (Linking Environment And Farming). Since the first Open Farm Sunday in 2006, over 1500 farmers across the UK have opened their gates and welcomed 1.8 million people onto their farm for one Sunday each year. It is an opportunity for everyone, young and old, to discover first hand what it means to be a farmer and the work they do producing food, enhancing the countryside and all the goods and services farmers provide. Each event is uniquely based around the farm’s individual story. Activities during the day may include a farm walk, nature trail, tractor and trailer rides, demonstrations, pond dipping, activities for children, a mini farmers market or farm shop. For the second year running, more than a quarter of a million people visited farms on Open Farm Sunday 5th June. Looking ahead to the future, LEAF launched a 10 year vision for Open Farm Sunday and Open Farm School Days in November 2014.

Whirlow Hall Farm is an Educational Trust which was set up in 1979 by Alan Aikin. Alan grew up in the inner city and was sent to a farm as an evacuee during the Second World War. He was so profoundly affected by his experience of farming and the countryside that years later he decided to set up a centre for all inner-city children to come and experience the wonders of the countryside and develop their understanding of where their food, farming and the countryside. Since that date, many thousands of children and young people have visited the Sheffield farm on a daily or residential basis. The Trust is a unique environmental and educational charity, providing an outstanding learning experience to over 10,000 children and young people a year, many of them from disadvantaged backgrounds and the inner city. For many young visitors this is the first time that they will have visited a farm or the countryside. By holding a newly-hatched chick, bottle feeding a new-born lamb or simply seeing a pig with her piglets for the first time they are having an unforgettable experience. Their educational visits and training range from nursery through to vocational and work-based learning.

Lynne's Organic Farm is an organic smallholding of just over 35 acres in the High Weald Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty near Eridge in East Sussex. The farm is fully organic, certified by the Soil Association since 2007. They produce organic pork, eggs and fruit and vegetables, all available in their small Farm Shop. One of their main aims is to farm in a sustainable and environmentally sound way.

Rainforest Saver are a charity promoting a technique called Inga alley cropping as a replacement for slash and burn farming in tropical rainforest areas. Currently they work with projects in Honduras and Cameroon. Slash and burn is an unsustainable agricultural technique practiced by 200 to 300 million tropical farmers worldwide, because that is the only way of making a living that they know. It means continuously cutting down the rainforests . Inga alley cropping is a successful alternative. It enables the farmer to make a better living without cutting down more forest. Rainforest Saver supports local, grassroots organisations to promote this better way of farming in practical ways.

Jimmy's Farm, as seen on TV, home of the rare breed Essex Pig. They are a working farm and are open for visitors 7 days a week. There's loads to do at the farm for a great family day out. They have a Nature Trail, Woodland Walk, Beautiful Garden's, Farm Shop, Adventure Play Area, Barn Restaurant and Field Kitchen. They sell all of their home reared free range pig produce, beef and lamb in their butchers as well as an abundance of herbs and veggies from their garden.

Founded in 1924, Biodynamic farming is the oldest 'green' farming movement, and forerunner of organics. All biodynamic farmers and growers practice organic methods of cultivation, are against genetic modification (GM), and share its ideals, but there are important differences. Biodynamics has metaphysical and spiritual roots that organics does not. Biodynamics thus embraces the mystery of all life processes, including the subtle and energetic realities that are not necessarily easy to measure or justify using current scientific methods.

Farms Not Factories is a non-profit organisation working through film-making and campaigning to support the ‘food sovereignty’ movement by exposing the true costs of cheap meat from animal factories in order to inspire people to only buy meat from local, healthy, high welfare farms. Our long term vision is a world without animal factories. Animal factories can be defined as indoor facilities in which overcrowding and lack of bedding means that the animals suffer stress and disease, are prone to tail biting and have to be routinely given antibiotics.

The UK Food Group is a network of around 50 development, environment, farmer and academic organisations in the UK working on global food and agriculture issues. The diversity of membership gives a unique, dynamic and holistic perspective on food and agriculture issues. Purpose The UK Food Group works to strengthen advocacy in the UK, the EU, the UN and other international bodies for a global food system that can achieve our vision. Solidarity They are in solidarity with the networks of those most vulnerable to hunger, including movements of small-scale farmers, herders and fishers in the global South. They support their right to be part of decision making in the global food system at all levels. Structural causes They always try to identify the underlying causes of problems in the global food system. Speaking out They want to let everyone know about the many great examples of sustainable and fair approaches to agriculture and local food systems that exist. They will also speak out against unjust and environmentally reckless approaches to food and agriculture.

LEAF (Linking Environment And Farming) is the leading organisation promoting sustainable agriculture, food and farming. We help farmers produce good food, with care and to high environmental standards, identified in-store by the LEAF Marque logo

Veggies is a volunteer-led, community-based, social enterprise. Veggies has been promoting vegan catering and supporting campaigns for human and animal rights, environmental protection and social justice since 1984. Veggies Catering Campaign provides catering at almost any event – from campaign rallies to community festivals, from family celebrations to green gatherings. They offer snacks, as well as information exploring the links between diet, animal suffering and the environment.

Anarchist Teapot are an anarchist collective that cooks at events which they want to support. They are predominantly based in Brighton but have cooked at events all over the country. They cook affordable, vegan, GM-free and mostly organic food. They don't aim to make profits. Anarchist Teapot formed out of a series of squatted cafes around Brighton, and have had a mobile kitchen since 1998.

Streets Kitchen was created as a grassroots space in order to create ll a central resource where anyone who is hungry, needing some info or anything that might help their situation can access information on food/soup runs. They work in partnership with other grassroots groups across the UK. They also create and support Street Kitchens. They are also attempting to list all the available Winter Shelters across the UK and Ireland urgently

The Sumac Centre is a volunteer-run social & community space based in Forest Fields, Nottingham. Established in 2001, the Sumac has been a hub for many people over the years. They currently have a cafe which is open every Saturday evening for a big communal meal called People’s Kitchen. The Sumac also provides resources and a meeting space for groups and individuals working to promote social justice, environmental awareness, peace, and animal rights. They support community resistance projects, as well as being the home to Nottingham Animal Rights and Veggies Catering Campaign. The Sumac also hosts regular community circle meetings. The space is sometimes used for music events, film showings and jumble sales in order to raise money and awareness. They organise co-operatively, without managers or bosses, and all volunteers have a say in how the centre is run. Open organising meetings are held on the first Monday of every month and operate by consensus. An aim is to provide a space where local people can meet other socially conscious individuals in a relaxed and friendly environment.

Drimlabarra Herb Farm on the Isle of Arran is situated at the southern end of one of Scotland’s most beautiful but accessible islands, they offer practical herbal medicine courses, individual herbal well being consultations and workshops in sustainable living. Established in 2000 by world recognised Traditional Medical Herbalists, Keith Robertson and Maureen Robertson, the farm is run on Veganic/Stockfree lines combining vegan (100% vegetarian) and organic philosophy. They are in effect, a Vegan sanctuary and retreat centre, dedicated to researching planetary health via herbal treatments, diet, cooking and raw food and practical hands-on green living. Their interest lies in community building and cooperation. They offer many ways people can participate through interactive learning including attendance at workshops, individual consultations, apprenticeships and open day visits

Sound Bites is an independent ethical wholefood shop and not-for-profit workers co-op, specialising in a wide range of vegetarian, vegan foods and free from foods – many of which are Fairtrade and/or organic. They began in 2005 to increase availability of ethical food and support positive social change in our local community.

Food Sovereignty Movement UK is inspired by the efforts of farmers and social movements around the world as well as action in the UK, working to build a movement for a democratic, sustainable and fair food system – food sovereignty.

Reclaim the Fields is a constellation of people and collective projects willing to go back to the land and reassume the control over food production. They are determined to create alternatives to capitalism through cooperative, collective, autonomous, real needs oriented small scale production and initiatives, putting theory into practice and linking local practical action with global political struggles.

This is Rubbish aims to communicate the preventable scale of food wasted in the UK, through policy research, community and arts led public events. Formed in 2009 by volunteers, TiR registered as a Community Interest Company in 2011. The organisation now has an extensive portfolio of successful events through England and Wales.

Community Food Growers Network is an informal network of people involved in community food growing in London. They share ideas, information and skills around the importance of growing food in the city, and campaign on issues important to us as food growers rooted in our local communities.

From obesity and diet-related ill-health to food poverty and waste, climate change and biodiversity loss to declining prosperity and social dislocation, food is not only at the heart of some of our greatest problems but is also a vital part of the solution. The Sustainable Food Cities approach involves developing a cross-sector partnership of local public agencies, businesses, academics and NGOs committed to working together to make healthy and sustainable food a defining characteristic of where they live. The Sustainable Food Cities Network helps people and places share challenges, explore practical solutions and develop best practice on key food issues.

Food Matters is a not-for-private-profit, national food policy and advocacy organisation. They encourage and support change towards sustainable, fair food systems. We all have our parts to play in taking action to create change within our food system, from communities, third-sector organisations and business through to local and national government. To support this change, Food Matters has developed an innovative, participatory, whole-food-systems approach to establishing healthy, sustainable, fair food as the norm.

Chagfarm (Chagford Community Farm CIC) aims to make the local community's food supply more resilient by working closely with Chagfood, another local food enterprise, and complementing their existing vegetable subscription offer. They do this by offering local goat dairy products and honey, as well as high-welfare goat meat, pork, organic woodland poultry, lamb, beef, venison and game. They operate on a payment by subscription basis, meaning customers sign up as members and commit to buying a certain amount of produce over a period of at least a year. Their mission is to develop a thriving local economy by supporting existing producers and retailers, including working with local butchers and offering produce from other farms.

Chagfood is one of a growing number of Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) schemes across the UK that directly connect consumers and the farmers who produce their food. CSA simply describes a model of subscription farming where customers commit to support a farm for an entire season by paying for their produce either up front or by monthly direct debit. From the farmer’s point of view this commitment provides a guaranteed market and allows us to farm in a more low-input ecological way. In return members have a direct connection to the people and the fields producing their food and the opportunity to get involved with how their food is produced. At Chagfood, they offer our members a ‘share’ of the harvest over the entire growing season for a set price. CSA is about consumers & farmers sharing the rewards and the risks of farming between them.

Whirlow Hall Farm is an Educational Trust which was set up in 1979 by Alan Aikin. Alan grew up in the inner city and was sent to a farm as an evacuee during the Second World War. He was so profoundly affected by his experience of farming and the countryside that years later he decided to set up a centre for all inner-city children to come and experience the wonders of the countryside and develop their understanding of where their food, farming and the countryside. Since that date, many thousands of children and young people have visited the Sheffield farm on a daily or residential basis. The Trust is a unique environmental and educational charity, providing an outstanding learning experience to over 10,000 children and young people a year, many of them from disadvantaged backgrounds and the inner city. For many young visitors this is the first time that they will have visited a farm or the countryside. By holding a newly-hatched chick, bottle feeding a new-born lamb or simply seeing a pig with her piglets for the first time they are having an unforgettable experience. Their educational visits and training range from nursery through to vocational and work-based learning.

SPEAK is a national network of students and young adults who campaign and pray on issues of global justice. They are a campaign and activist company, charity and participatory network that aims to bring change. SPEAK began with Christian roots but in recent years has been working through side partnerships and networks.

Farms Not Factories is a non-profit organisation working through film-making and campaigning to support the ‘food sovereignty’ movement by exposing the true costs of cheap meat from animal factories in order to inspire people to only buy meat from local, healthy, high welfare farms. Our long term vision is a world without animal factories. Animal factories can be defined as indoor facilities in which overcrowding and lack of bedding means that the animals suffer stress and disease, are prone to tail biting and have to be routinely given antibiotics.

Whole Food Action host a map of independent wholefood shops. They see these shops as part of a movement towards a food system that is fair, healthy, and ecologically sustainable. We also think they have a big role to play in campaigning for such a system. Their site is intended to: locate indie wholefood shops around the UK get informed and campaign for food sovereignty be inspired to set up a new shop or co-op!

The UK Food Group is a network of around 50 development, environment, farmer and academic organisations in the UK working on global food and agriculture issues. The diversity of membership gives a unique, dynamic and holistic perspective on food and agriculture issues. Purpose The UK Food Group works to strengthen advocacy in the UK, the EU, the UN and other international bodies for a global food system that can achieve our vision. Solidarity They are in solidarity with the networks of those most vulnerable to hunger, including movements of small-scale farmers, herders and fishers in the global South. They support their right to be part of decision making in the global food system at all levels. Structural causes They always try to identify the underlying causes of problems in the global food system. Speaking out They want to let everyone know about the many great examples of sustainable and fair approaches to agriculture and local food systems that exist. They will also speak out against unjust and environmentally reckless approaches to food and agriculture.

FoodCycle is a charity which organises volunteers, surplus food and spare kitchen spaces to create nutritious meals for people at risk of food poverty and social isolation. The Food Research Collaboration (FRC) is the only initiative in the UK dedicated to bringing together academics and Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) working to improve the UK food system. An initiative of the Centre for Food Policy (CFP) at City, University of London, their mission is to facilitate more effective collaboration between academics and CSOs to produce, share and use the knowledge needed to improve UK food policy. Their longer term vision is of academic and CSO communities working better together to influence and improve UK food policy to build a healthier, more sustainable food system. The FRC comprises a Secretariat (a team of three, chaired by Prof Corinna Hawkes and supported by Founder and Special Advisor Prof Tim Lang, all based at the CFP); a Steering Group (representing 6 universities and 7 NGOs); and the Membership (over 500 individuals from 123 CSOs and 97 universities working on a wide range of food issues across the UK).

The Nutrition Society was established in 1941 ‘to advance the scientific study of nutrition and its application to the maintenance of human and animal health'. Highly regarded by the scientific community, the Society is the largest learned society for nutrition in Europe. The Society is a not for profit, membership organisation. Those with a genuine interest in the science of human or animal nutrition can become a member. Membership is worldwide with a majority of members living in UK and Europe. The Nutrition Society: •publishes five renowned journals consisting of highly regarded scientific research •creates and organises CPD accredited conferences disseminating cutting-edge nutrition science and attracting nutrition scientists •works with industry representatives and researchers from the around the world •offers CPD accredited training workshops to enhance and develop skills •creates opportunities to network and develop relationships with like-minded individuals and communities •publishes six highly regarded textbooks •offers up to date news in areas of nutrition research.

Titbits specialises in gourmet vegan and raw living cuisine. Their mission is to provide healthy, creative and delicious plant based foods with high quality, ethically sourced ingredients. Brighton-based catering business, who also do cookery classes.

The Sumac Centre is a volunteer-run social & community space based in Forest Fields, Nottingham. Established in 2001, the Sumac has been a hub for many people over the years. They currently have a cafe which is open every Saturday evening for a big communal meal called People’s Kitchen. The Sumac also provides resources and a meeting space for groups and individuals working to promote social justice, environmental awareness, peace, and animal rights. They support community resistance projects, as well as being the home to Nottingham Animal Rights and Veggies Catering Campaign. The Sumac also hosts regular community circle meetings. The space is sometimes used for music events, film showings and jumble sales in order to raise money and awareness. They organise co-operatively, without managers or bosses, and all volunteers have a say in how the centre is run. Open organising meetings are held on the first Monday of every month and operate by consensus. An aim is to provide a space where local people can meet other socially conscious individuals in a relaxed and friendly environment.

Drimlabarra Herb Farm on the Isle of Arran is situated at the southern end of one of Scotland’s most beautiful but accessible islands, they offer practical herbal medicine courses, individual herbal well being consultations and workshops in sustainable living. Established in 2000 by world recognised Traditional Medical Herbalists, Keith Robertson and Maureen Robertson, the farm is run on Veganic/Stockfree lines combining vegan (100% vegetarian) and organic philosophy. They are in effect, a Vegan sanctuary and retreat centre, dedicated to researching planetary health via herbal treatments, diet, cooking and raw food and practical hands-on green living. Their interest lies in community building and cooperation. They offer many ways people can participate through interactive learning including attendance at workshops, individual consultations, apprenticeships and open day visits

They began in 2005 to increase availability of ethical food and support positive social change in our local community.

Green Fork seeks to give people access to healthy, fresh and great tasting food and supply in a way that is convenient. They strive to serve great food that is nutritious, fresh and where possible locally produced, whilst maintaining a ruthless food hygiene standard and will deliver direct to offices for maximum convenience, free of charge and using innovative ways that leaves no carbon footprint. They deliver food to offices in both Exchange Quays and Salford Quays. We provide companies with great quality, fresh sandwiches, Lunch Pots and smoothies. All of their food is made fresh the same morning and is designed to be healthy, delicious and office friendly. They have also recently opened their first deli bar located in Trafford Park, Manchester.

The Nutrition Society was established in 1941 ‘to advance the scientific study of nutrition and its application to the maintenance of human and animal health'. Highly regarded by the scientific community, the Society is the largest learned society for nutrition in Europe. The Society is a not for profit, membership organisation. Those with a genuine interest in the science of human or animal nutrition can become a member. Membership is worldwide with a majority of members living in UK and Europe. The Nutrition Society: •publishes five renowned journals consisting of highly regarded scientific research •creates and organises CPD accredited conferences disseminating cutting-edge nutrition science and attracting nutrition scientists •works with industry representatives and researchers from the around the world •offers CPD accredited training workshops to enhance and develop skills •creates opportunities to network and develop relationships with like-minded individuals and communities •publishes six highly regarded textbooks •offers up to date news in areas of nutrition research.

The Association for Nutrition (AfN) defines and advances standards of evidence-based practice across the field of nutrition and at all levels within the workforce. They protect and benefit the public by: •Championing Registrants (ANutrs/RNutrs) whose entry onto the UK Voluntary Register of Nutritionists (UKVRN) is an assurance that they meet our rigorous standards of competence and professionalism. •Recognising high quality, relevant nutrition training through their Degree Programme Accreditation, CPD Endorsement and Certification schemes. •Raising their profile to protect the public and raise demand for, and recognition of, the contribution of Registered Nutritionists and the wider workforce in nutrition.

The BNF brings together those with an interest in food and nutrition from diverse sectors - academia, medicine, education, communication and the food chain.

Formed in 2009 by volunteers, TiR registered as a Community Interest Company in 2011. The organisation now has an extensive portfolio of successful events through England and Wales.

Community Food Growers Network is an informal network of people involved in community food growing in London. They share ideas, information and skills around the importance of growing food in the city, and campaign on issues important to us as food growers rooted in our local communities.

From obesity and diet-related ill-health to food poverty and waste, climate change and biodiversity loss to declining prosperity and social dislocation, food is not only at the heart of some of our greatest problems but is also a vital part of the solution. The Sustainable Food Cities approach involves developing a cross-sector partnership of local public agencies, businesses, academics and NGOs committed to working together to make healthy and sustainable food a defining characteristic of where they live. The Sustainable Food Cities Network helps people and places share challenges, explore practical solutions and develop best practice on key food issues.

We all have our parts to play in taking action to create change within our food system, from communities, third-sector organisations and business through to local and national government. To support this change, Food Matters has developed an innovative, participatory, whole-food-systems approach to establishing healthy, sustainable, fair food as the norm.

targets.Description: Chagfarm (Chagford Community Farm CIC) aims to make the local community's food supply more resilient by working closely with Chagfood, another local food enterprise, and complementing their existing vegetable subscription offer. They do this by offering local goat dairy products and honey, as well as high-welfare goat meat, pork, organic woodland poultry, lamb, beef, venison and game. They operate on a payment by subscription basis, meaning customers sign up as members and commit to buying a certain amount of produce over a period of at least a year. Their mission is to develop a thriving local economy by supporting existing producers and retailers, including working with local butchers and offering produce from other farms.

Chagfood is one of a growing number of Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) schemes across the UK that directly connect consumers and the farmers who produce their food. CSA simply describes a model of subscription farming where customers commit to support a farm for an entire season by paying for their produce either up front or by monthly direct debit. From the farmer’s point of view this commitment provides a guaranteed market and allows us to farm in a more low-input ecological way. In return members have a direct connection to the people and the fields producing their food and the opportunity to get involved with how their food is produced. At Chagfood, they offer our members a ‘share’ of the harvest over the entire growing season for a set price. CSA is about consumers & farmers sharing the rewards and the risks of farming between them.

Chantry Farm is a campsite in the South East of England, consisting of 54 acres on the South Downs. They promote walks in the country to see skylarks, sheep and other guests. The campers help fund the farm restoration. Chantry dates back to 1350. Campers also help fund Chantry Farm to undertake small scale local food production.

LEAF Open Farm Sunday, is managed by LEAF (Linking Environment And Farming). Since the first Open Farm Sunday in 2006, over 1500 farmers across the UK have opened their gates and welcomed 1.8 million people onto their farm for one Sunday each year. It is an opportunity for everyone, young and old, to discover first hand what it means to be a farmer and the work they do producing food, enhancing the countryside and all the goods and services farmers provide. Each event is uniquely based around the farm’s individual story. Activities during the day may include a farm walk, nature trail, tractor and trailer rides, demonstrations, pond dipping, activities for children, a mini farmers market or farm shop. For the second year running, more than a quarter of a million people visited farms on Open Farm Sunday 5th June. Looking ahead to the future, LEAF launched a 10 year vision for Open Farm Sunday and Open Farm School Days in November 2014.

Whirlow Hall Farm is an Educational Trust which was set up in 1979 by Alan Aikin. Alan grew up in the inner city and was sent to a farm as an evacuee during the Second World War. He was so profoundly affected by his experience of farming and the countryside that years later he decided to set up a centre for all inner-city children to come and experience the wonders of the countryside and develop their understanding of where their food, farming and the countryside. Since that date, many thousands of children and young people have visited the Sheffield farm on a daily or residential basis. The Trust is a unique environmental and educational charity, providing an outstanding learning experience to over 10,000 children and young people a year, many of them from disadvantaged backgrounds and the inner city. For many young visitors this is the first time that they will have visited a farm or the countryside. By holding a newly-hatched chick, bottle feeding a new-born lamb or simply seeing a pig with her piglets for the first time they are having an unforgettable experience. Their educational visits and training range from nursery through to vocational and work-based learning.

Lynne's Organic Farm is an organic smallholding of just over 35 acres in the High Weald Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty near Eridge in East Sussex. The farm is fully organic, certified by the Soil Association since 2007. They produce organic pork, eggs and fruit and vegetables, all available in their small Farm Shop. One of their main aims is to farm in a sustainable and environmentally sound way.

Rainforest Saver are a charity promoting a technique called Inga alley cropping as a replacement for slash and burn farming in tropical rainforest areas. Currently they work with projects in Honduras and Cameroon. Slash and burn is an unsustainable agricultural technique practiced by 200 to 300 million tropical farmers worldwide, because that is the only way of making a living that they know. It means continuously cutting down the rainforests . Inga alley cropping is a successful alternative. It enables the farmer to make a better living without cutting down more forest. Rainforest Saver supports local, grassroots organisations to promote this better way of farming in practical ways.

Jimmy's Farm, as seen on TV, home of the rare breed Essex Pig. They are a working farm and are open for visitors 7 days a week. There's loads to do at the farm for a great family day out. They have a Nature Trail, Woodland Walk, Beautiful Garden's, Farm Shop, Adventure Play Area, Barn Restaurant and Field Kitchen. They sell all of their home reared free range pig produce, beef and lamb in their butchers as well as an abundance of herbs and veggies from their garden.

SPEAK is a national network of students and young adults who campaign and pray on issues of global justice. They are a campaign and activist company, charity and participatory network that aims to bring change. SPEAK began with Christian roots but in recent years has been working through side partnerships and networks.

Founded in 1924, Biodynamic farming is the oldest 'green' farming movement, and forerunner of organics. All biodynamic farmers and growers practice organic methods of cultivation, are against genetic modification (GM), and share its ideals, but there are important differences. Biodynamics has metaphysical and spiritual roots that organics does not. Biodynamics thus embraces the mystery of all life processes, including the subtle and energetic realities that are not necessarily easy to measure or justify using current scientific methods.

Farms Not Factories is a non-profit organisation working through film-making and campaigning to support the ‘food sovereignty’ movement by exposing the true costs of cheap meat from animal factories in order to inspire people to only buy meat from local, healthy, high welfare farms. Our long term vision is a world without animal factories. Animal factories can be defined as indoor facilities in which overcrowding and lack of bedding means that the animals suffer stress and disease, are prone to tail biting and have to be routinely given antibiotics.

Whole Food Action host a map of independent wholefood shops. They see these shops as part of a movement towards a food system that is fair, healthy, and ecologically sustainable. The UK Food Group is a network of around 50 development, environment, farmer and academic organisations in the UK working on global food and agriculture issues. The diversity of membership gives a unique, dynamic and holistic perspective on food and agriculture issues. Purpose The UK Food Group works to strengthen advocacy in the UK, the EU, the UN and other international bodies for a global food system that can achieve our vision. Solidarity They are in solidarity with the networks of those most vulnerable to hunger, including movements of small-scale farmers, herders and fishers in the global South. They support their right to be part of decision making in the global food system at all levels. Structural causes They always try to identify the underlying causes of problems in the global food system. Speaking out They want to let everyone know about the many great examples of sustainable and fair approaches to agriculture and local food systems that exist. They will also speak out against unjust and environmentally reckless approaches to food and agriculture.

The website for the In The Welsh Wind Distillery, makers of bespoke spirits in their 50 litre copper pot still, Meredith. Also hosting Gin making workshops and events at their licensed bar all in the distillery. In The Welsh Wind Distillery is located at Tresaith in West Wales.

The website for Distyllfa Llanfairpwll Distillery, a small batch distillery from the village of Llanfair­pwllgwyngyll­gogery­chwyrn­drobwll­llan­tysilio­gogo­goch on The Isle of Anglesey off the coast of North West Wales. The company is aiming to create genuine craft distilled spirits using as many botanicals grown on Anglesey as they can.
Streets Kitchen is a UK & Ireland grassroots group working to help the homeless community, providing daily outreaches with food, clothing and information that benefits our streets.

The website for Chapel 1877, a vibrant restaurant in Cardiff. Three floors of luxurious surroundings, themed on the renovated Chapel first constructed in 1877. The French-Italian Gothic themed creation was originally designed by the architect Henry C Harris, renowned for his incredible structures throughout Cardiff and Wales in the late 1800s.

The website of Barti Rum, launched in 2017, an idea captured by Jonathan Williams, seaweed fanatic and founder of The Pembrokeshire Beach Food Company. Barti Rum is made up of a blend of the finest Caribbean rum, seasoned with not only the most vibrant notes of vanilla, clove and subtle orange, but with hand picked laver seaweed from the beautiful Pembrokeshire coast.

The website for Bluestone Brewing, an exciting, eco-friendly family run brewery situated in the foothills of the Preseli Hills in North Pembrokeshire. Producing hand crafted real ales, using local water filtered down through the Bluestone Hills to produce a range of flavoursome Rock Solid Ales.

The website for Brecon Brewing, founded in 2011 Brecon Brewing quickly established a reputation as one of Wales' best known breweries with one of Wales' best known brewers Buster Grant at the helm, Brecon Brewing have created a range of beers full of flavour and character inspired by the dramatic Brecon Beacons.
The website for Cerddin Brewery, based in Maesteg where all the beer that is produced comes from green energy.

The website for Conwy Brewery, the first brewery in Conwy for over 100 years when it was established in 2003. Specialising in cask & bottle conditioned ales of the highest quality with probably the best range of ales in North Wales.

The website for the Neuadd Arms Hotel and Brewery, a hotel which has stood in the centre of Llanwrtyd Wells for over 145 years with 19th century character, complete with open log fires in the lounge and public bars. And a brewery established in 2004 using local spring water and based in the renovated derelict stables situated behind the Neuadd Arms Hotel.

targets.Description: The website for the Glamorgan Brewing Company, based in Llantrisant. The Anstee family began supplying the hospitality trade in South Wales with beers, wines and spirits in the early 90’s. The knowledge and community ties established during this time gave them a real desire to see quality Welsh beer back on local bars. So much so they thought they’d brew some themselves.
The website for Monty's Brewery, an award winning brewery based near Montgomery, Powys, in the heart of Mid Wales.

The website for Y Bragdy Mws Piws | The Purple Moose Brewery, a '40-Barrel' micro-brewery based in the historic harbour town of Porthmadog, North Wales, close to the mountains of Snowdonia. Brewing commenced on 14th June 2005 with a one-off special pale ale at 3.5% called "No.1".
targets.Title of Target: Y Bragdy Mws Piws | The Purple Moose Brewery

targets.Description: The website for Tudor Brewery, an award winning family run company based in Llanhilleth, Nr. Abertillery, Wales and following the model of a cottage industry. They have achieved the highest accolade of Three Gold Stars as the Great Taste Awards. This is run by the Guild of Fine Foods and has been stated as the Oscars of the Food and Drink Industry.

The website for Felinfoel Brewery, situated in ‘Felinfoel’, a small village adjoining Llanelli in Wales. Historians tell us that in the old days the inn brewed its own beer, but only during the winter months. The keeping qualities and the strength of the beers, therefore, were of prime importance and the popularity of ‘Felinfoel Beer’ led to the local inn brewing for other inns in the locality. This, in turn, led to the present brewery being built in 1878 to accommodate demand.
The website for Tiny Rebel Brewing, an award winning brewery located in Rogerstone, South Wales.

The website for the Crafty Devil Brewing Company, esablished in 2014 by best mates Adam Edinborough & Rhys Watkins in Rhys' then Garden Shed in west Cardiff. Crafty Devil Brewing are Cardiff's alternative to the corporate mass producing breweries. An independent and proud Cardiff Brewery Crafty Devil Brewing are now brewing in Ninian Park Road, Canton, Cardiff.
The website for the Geipel Brewery, a microbrewery specialising in bottom-fermented beers, more commonly known as lagers. Founded in 2013 in North Wales.

The website for the Lines Brew Company, formed in 2016 around an eco-conscientious, locally sourced ethos to develop innovative beer steeped in history, brewed along dragon lines, using fresh running water from their own source in house. Based in Caerphilly, Wales.
The website for the Tenby Brewing Company, an independent craft brewer in the beautiful harbour town of Tenby.

The website for the Apple County Cider Company, a family business, run jointly by Ben and Steph. The apple trees at Whitehouse Farm were planted in the 60's by Ben's stepfather Jimmy who experimented with making his own real cider and encouraged Ben to join him. In 2008 Ben answered his calling and decided to move back to the family farm to become a full-time cider maker, Ben is incredibly passionate about cider and has always been a cider-drinker, in 2014 Apple County Cider was born.
The website for Gwynt y Ddraig, cider and perry makers established in 2001 and based in Llantwit Fardre, South Wales..
The website for Hallets Cider, founded by Andy and Annie Hallett and producing handmade real cider produced at Blaengawney Farm in South Wales.

The website for the Celtic Spirit Company, producing spirits and liqueur drinks from age old Welsh family recipes dating back to the 1870s. These spirits and liqueurs are derived from fruits of the Wye and Usk Valleys. Early spirit drinks were enhanced at Llanthony Priory by the addition of fruit, herbs and spices to flavour ‘cordials’, used as pick-me-ups and stimulants.

The website for Condessa Welsh Liqueurs - Richard Jones started his Condessa business in Chester in 1969. In 1989 the business moved to a 5,400 sq. ft. liqueur factory and winery in rural Anglesey and now make award winning fruit liqueurs and low fat cream liqueurs.

The website of Ancre Hill Estates, a winery located in the Welsh county of Monmouthshire. The 12 hectares of vineyards are perfectly positioned on south facing slopes close to the border town of Monmouth and the Wye Valley (AONB).

The website for White Castle Vineyard, owned by Robb & Nicola Merchant, it is situated in the beautiful rolling countryside of Monmouthshire in the village of Llanvetherine close to the towns of Abergavenny and Monmouth. The 7 acre vineyard is planted on gentle slopes that are ideal for growing vines and ripening grapes for Welsh wine.
The website for The Pembrokeshire Beachfood Company, an ethical seafood supplier specialising in seaweed and laverbread recipes and products.

The website for Coaltown Coffee Roasters, a business established up with one ambition, to bring an industry back to their hometown. All Coaltown coffee is roasted and packed at their roastery on Foundry Road, Ammanford where they employ local people to bring them into the world of third-wave coffee.

The website for Tan Y Castell Bakery, Pembrokeshire - the creation of Paul and Linda Mear. Paul started producing our famous Welshcakes at the family farm using an old Aga and then selling them to local shops around his farm. Today, Tan Y Castell has three large purpose-built bakeries spread over 6 industrial units and employs over 100 full-time staff.
The website for Clam’s Cakes, a multiple award winning bakery based in South Wales.

The website for Princes Gate Mineral Water, founded on an organic farm in a remote corner of Pembrokeshire with David and Glyn Jones and their parents bottling Princes Gate water by hand. It started as an experiment in the family’s efforts to diversify their farming practices and now they are one of the largest suppliers in Wales. Princes gate focus on environmental concerns and have lead the way with introducing recycled materials into their bottling process.
The website for The Welsh Cheese Company, aiming to be a showcase for some of the best artisan cheese makers in Wales.
The website for Hafod Welsh Organic Cheddar. Hafod is a traditional hard cheese handmade on Wales’ longest certified organic dairy farm, Bwlchwernen Fawr.

The website for Pant Mawr Farmhouse Cheeses, a family business is run by David, Cynthia and Jason Jennings at their small traditional Welsh Hill Farm located in the foothills of the Preseli Mountains at Rosebush in Pembrokeshire. Pant Mawr Cheeses have been developed using locally produced milk, they combine their self-taught skills and unique self-developed recipes to produce a range of mouth watering, traditional hand mad cheeses.
The website for the Drop Bear Beer Company, a Swansea based brewery committed to creating revolutionary craft beers below 0.5% ABV.

The website for Bug Farm Foods, set up by husband and wife team entomologist (insect scientist) Dr Sarah Beynon and chef (food wizard) Andy Holcroft. Together they’ve developed a new generation of insect-based foods to help tackle issues of sustainability in the food chain. From their base in wild West Wales, their aim is to bring you sustainable and delicious food.

The website for The Bug Farm, where farming practice is informed by scientific research. Working with a number of universities, they have a programme of research that covers all aspects of the food chain: farming edible insects for food and feed; farming native insects for land management purposes; and using the services bugs provide to farm more efficiently. Based in St. Davids, Pembrokeshire.
The website for Discover Delicious, a hub for some of the finest Welsh food and drink with a collection of award-winning produce from a selection of the very best Welsh artisan producers.

The website for the Gwaun Valley Brewery. Len Davies began brewing by making homebrew in the farmhouse kitchen when he came to live in the Gwaun Valley in Pembrokeshire, West Wales. Perfecting his recipes became his passion and the beers they offer are the result of many hours of diligent experimentation to get the unique and delicious flavours.
The website for Cwm Deri Vineyard, based in Pembrokeshire and offering a restaurant, camping and Glamping, wine tasting etc as part of their vineyard business.

The website for Gower Brewery, using, old fashioned, traditional methods under Master Brewer Dave Campbell, the brewery is spreading the word of craft beer around the country and put Gower on the map as a destination for great beer.
The website for the Tomos Watkin Brewery, a family run, award winning brewery based in Swansea, South Wales.

The website for Glyndŵr Vineyard, the oldest and largest established vineyard in Wales. The current owners pioneered the revival of viticulture in Wales, establishing Glyndwr Vineyard in 1979, making it the oldest family estate in Wales.
The website for Llanerch, a stylish farmhouse in the Welsh countryside with rooms, restaurant, cookery school, and vineyard.
The website for Parva Farm and Vineyard, a privately owned and run vineyard in the village of Tintern, South Wales, producing award-winning wines, meads and sparkling wines for all occasions.

The website for the Sugar Loaf Vineyards, set in area of outstanding natural beauty in the Brecon Beacons National Park and panoramic views over the Usk Valley, with 7 varieties of grapes planted on 5 acres of south facing slopes this ensures excellent ripening of the grapes, while the balanced soils add a special character to the wine.

The website for Williams Brothers Cider, a small, family run business producing high quality, hand crafted, award winning, traditional real Welsh cider. These multi award winning ciders are carefully handmade, using traditional methods, at their dedicated cider house facility in Caerphilly county, South Wales.

The website for Bragdy Dinbych - Denbigh Brewery, established in early 2012 following a non-too-serious discussion in the Vaults one evening. Attempting to counter the cheap supermaket offers by offering modest quantities of real ale, delivered to you door locally, and at prices that compare favourably with supermarkets.
The website for Welsh Mountain Cider, a small scale real cider producers in mid-Wales.

The website for Cwm Rhondda Ales, brewed using traditional methods and are bottled by hand. Cwm Rhondda Ales promotes environmental sustainability in every aspect of their work. They use the water from their very own natural spring and the waste from the brewing process has even proved ideal food for the farm’s cattle!

The website for Pontypridd Foodbank | Banc Bwyd Pontypridd, providing three days’ nutritionally balanced emergency food and support to local people who are referred to us in crisis. They are part of a nationwide network of foodbanks, supported by The Trussell Trust, working to combat poverty and hunger across the UK.

The website for the Restaurant James Sommerin, a Michelin star restaurant situated on the esplanade in Penarth, Wales. The restaurant has the luxury of having panoramic views over the Severn Estuary which sets the scene for a very relaxing dining experience.

The website for The Hardwick, Abergavenny, Stephen Terry’s stellar Welsh pub is a favourite dining spot for the country’s foodie elite, garnering rave reviews from the likes of Masterchef’s Greg Wallace and a whole host of other national restaurant critics.

The website for Sosban and The Old Butcher’s, a restaurant located in the heart of Menai Bridge on the Isle of Anglesey, within a historical Butcher’s Shop, their dining experience is a little different to most. They create a series of dishes using the best locally sourced produce available to us on the day providing a unique culinary journey not found anywhere else.

The website for Tyddyn Llan, a restaurant in rural North Wales, near Chester, Llangollen and Wrexham. Holding a Michelin star since 2010 and well-rated in the ‘Good Food Guide’ coming 36th in the ‘Sunday Times’ Top 100 restaurants.

The website for The Whitebrook, a restaurant near Monmouth, Wales. Chris Harrod, chef patron, and his wife Kirsty, manage a stylish restaurant with rooms. Their emphasis is on an experience of excellence throughout. They have already won a clutch of awards, including a Michelin star and 4 AA Rosettes.

The website for The Checkers, Montgomery, a Michelin-star restaurant offering accommodation. Chef proprietor Stéphane Borie hails from Agen, near Bordeaux and - together with his partner Sarah - creates some of the finest dishes in Wales. Sarah's sister Kathryn - who runs front of house - completes the family business line-up and together they are locally known as 'the Frenchman and the farmers daughters'.

The website for The Walnut Tree, Llanddewi Skirrid. A famous, Michelin star inn and restaurant since the early 60’s, The Walnut Tree sits two miles east of Abergavenny. The food is an eclectic mix, based on Shaun Hill’s personal taste, paired with sound cooking techniques; rather than a particular country's cuisine. A unifying feature is the core of excellent ingredients.
The website for Ynyshir, a destination Michelin star restaurant with rooms located on the coast of mid-Wales near the Snowdonia National Park.

The website for Luke Thomas, a chef with an insatiable appetite for spinning classic dishes into contemporary British fare, he opened Gin Rickey’s in Chester in 2014, followed by a pop up diner concept, Retro Feasts in Mayfair, which launched successfully in Dubai in 2015. He also managed to squeeze in publishing a cookbook with Penguin titled Luke’s Cookbook and cooking on TV shows in the UK and now moving into the USA too, from show’s such as ITV’s This Morning, Great British Menu, Junior MasterChef and Chopped on Food Network.

The website for Aber Food Surplus, a pioneering not-for-profit social enterprise focused on tackling food waste and delivering meaningful community change. They collect the food local businesses are throwing away and redistribute it among the community. Through Pay As You Feel meals, they bring local people together and show them ‘waste’ food can be tasty and nutritious.

The website for HARBWR, Tenby Harbour Brewery is a family business established in 2015, and situated in refurbished premises in Sergeants Lane. Steeped in history, the brewery is designed to portray the rich heritage of Tenby as a seaside town, before bringing guests up-to-date with HARBWR Brewery’s modern tastes.

The website for the Good Grub Club, a co-operative of independent businesses from the retail, hospitality, farming and food sectors in and around the Dee Valley, North Wales. We offer networking, training and events. Aiming to increase the availability of food raised, grown or made in their region, provide training and mentoring for local young people keen to work in the food and drink sector, and improve the quality of the visitor experience to the Dee Valley.

The website for the Brecknock Hill Cheviot Sheep Society. The Brecknock Hill Cheviot has developed from the Scottish Cheviot that was introducted into Brecknockshire, Wales during the latter part of the 19th Century. This new strain of Cheviot thrives on exposed hills because of it’s hardiness. Not only are they kept as pure flocks for breeding purposes they can be successfully crossed with native Welsh Hill breeds.

The website for the Kerry Hill Sheep Society. The Kerry Hill is a breed of domestic sheep originating in the county of Powys in Wales. It derives its name from the village of Kerry (Ceri), near Newtown. Kerry Hill sheep have a distinctive and unique coloration, with a white face bearing black markings around the mouth, ears, and eyes.

The website for The Welsh Mountain Sheep Society. The Society has over 400 members, farming in some of the most difficult areas in Wales where it is essential to keep a special breed of sheep that is able to withstand the difficult climatic conditions. These sheep are the Welsh Mountain, a breed dating back to the Middle Ages, but one that is as relevant now and for the future as it ever was in the past. Unrivalled in its natural upland environment, its intrinsic qualities make it an ideal breed for lowland farms also.
The website for Pysgod Cymru, the online resource for the Ceredigion and Pembrokeshire Fisheries Local Action Groups.

The website for Pontcanna Farmers' Market, based in Cardiff and held every Saturday. Offering fresh food and supporting local artisan traders and farmers in Wales along with those offering interesting produces from around Europe and the world. Also hosting street food events every second Saturday.

The website for Cowny Mussels, a company based in Conwy, North Wales that is harvesting and supplying mussels using traditional methods rather than modern production techniques. They hand-rake wild mussels from small wooden boats, a practice passed down through three generations.

The website for The Gourmet Gardener, a plant nursery and productive kitchen garden based in a 2 acre Victorian Walled Garden just outside Abergavenny. Using fresh ingredients they make a range of seasonally flavoured condiments including, preserves, cordials, pickles and ferments.

Everything is done naturally using methods that support and nourish the land and plants, using no agrichemicals detrimental to human, animal or plant health.

The website for Parsons Pickles, originally established in Laugharne, Carmarthenshire in 1947. Now based at Burry Port, Wales and producing a range of quality traditional pickles together with its popular and well established laverbread and shellfish products.

The website for The Preservation Society, an award winning Chepstow based company making jams and preserves using the traditional 'open pan' method. Ethically aware they are using only recycled and recyclable packaging and offering a deposit on all jars sold, 10p when you return the jar to the shop.

The website for Usk River Natural Preserves, an Abergavenny based company making preserves by hand using traditional techniques, patient cooking and all-natural ingredients, often sourced locally as the seasons turn.

The website for Penarth Vineyard, the home of Penarth Estate Welsh Wines, based in Newtown, Montgomeryshire. Yet these grapes are grown outside and face the elements giving them a richness of flavours and depth of character.

The website for Dylan's Restaurants, these waterside restaurants are dotted along the North Wales coastline, currently with sites at Criccieth, Menai Bridge and Llandudno serving fresh local produce in beautiful locations. targets.Description: The National Food Strategy is the first independent review of England’s entire food system for 75 years. It aims to ensure that our food system: 1) Delivers safe, healthy, affordable food, regardless of where people live or how much they earn; 2) Is robust in the face of future shocks; 3) Restores and enhances the natural environment for the next generation in this country; 4) Is built upon a resilient, sustainable and humane agriculture sector; 5) Is a thriving contributor to our urban and rural economies, delivering well paid jobs and supporting innovative producers and manufacturers across the country; and 6) Delivers all this in an efficient and cost-effective way. Part 1 contains urgent recommendations to support the country through the turbulence caused by the COVID-19 pandemic

The land on which Black Pool Mill sits was once part of the Slebech Estate, which in the 11th Century was gifted to the Knights Hospitallers of the Order of St John.
